He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green Falcons]]. ==High school career== Plowden is a native of [[Germantown, Philadelphia]], and attended Mastery Charter North School. He was the school's first 1,000-point scorer and was a two-time all-state team selection. Plowden played primarily as a [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] and [[center (basketball)|center]] in high school;{{cite web|first=Josh|last=Verlin|title=Plowden impresses back home in college debut|url=https://www.cityofbasketballlove.com/news_article/show/855255|work=City of Basketball Love|date=November 11, 2017|access-date=September 16, 2022}} he credits his team's coaches, Terrence Cook and Gerald Johnson, for teaching him combined [[Big man (basketball)|big man]] and [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] skills.{{cite web|first=Donald|last=Hunt|title=Mastery Charter star shines with Bowling Green|url=https://www.phillytrib.com/sports/basketball/mastery-charter-star-shines-with-bowling-green/article_1b9489fb-5739-5cac-ade1-4ea58604cfcc.html|work=The Philadelphia Tribune|date=February 18, 2021|access-date=September 16, 2022}} On November 9, 2016, Plowden signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for the [[Bowling Green Falcons men's basketball|Bowling Green Falcons]].{{cite web|first=Aaron|last=Carter|title=Mastery's Plowden to play next at Bowling Green|url=https://www.inquirer.com/philly/sports/high_school/20161110_Mastery_s_Plowden_to_play_next_at_Bowling_Green.html|work=The Philadelphia Inquirer|date=November 10, 2016|access-date=September 16, 2022}} [[ESPN]] ranked him as the 20th best player in [[Pennsylvania]] in his recruiting class.{{cite web|first=J. Patrick|last=Eaken|title=Plowden’s progress: BGSU senior grew into star basketball player|url=https://www.sent-trib.com/sports/plowden-s-progress-bgsu-senior-grew-into-star-basketball-player/article_15008b2c-a20c-11ec-bd1a-e737603cfbb6.html|work=Sentinel-Tribune|date=March 12, 2022|access-date=September 16, 2022}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ==College career== Plowden was named to the All-[[Mid-American Conference]] (MAC) second-team in 2020 and the third-team in 2021 and 2022.{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Crisan|title=Plowden's versatility, energy could translate to NBA|url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/bgsu/2022/06/22/plowden-s-versatility-energy-could-translate-to-nba/stories/20220622022|work=Toledo Blade|date=June 23, 2022|access-date=September 16, 2022}} He was selected to the MAC All-Defensive team in 2022. Plowden finished his career with the Falcons with 1,618 points and 935 rebounds. He did not miss a game during his college career and is the program leader in games played with 154. ==Professional career== ===Birmingham Squadron (2022–2023)=== Plowden worked out with the [[Washington Wizards]], [[New Orleans Pelicans]] and [[Utah Jazz]] prior to the [[2022 NBA draft]] but went undrafted.{{cite web|first=Corey|last=Crisan|title=Bowling Green's Daeqwon Plowden goes undrafted|url=https://www.toledoblade.com/sports/bgsu/2022/06/23/bowlng-green-s-daeqwon-plowden-goes-undrafted/stories/20220623164|work=Toledo Blade|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=September 16, 2022}} He joined the Pelicans for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]] and averaged 12 points per game.{{cite web|first=Owen|last=McCue|title=Mastery North product Daeqwon Plowden hopes for NBA shot with Pelicans|url=https://www.cityofbasketballlove.com/news_article/show/1234090|work=City of Basketball Love|date=July 29, 2022|access-date=September 16, 2022}} On September 9, 2022, Plowden signed with the Pelicans,{{cite web|title=Pelicans sign Seabron, Petty Jr., and Plowden|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-roster-dereon-seabron-john-petty-jr-daeqwon-plowden-signed|website=NBA.com|date=September 9, 2022|access-date=September 16, 2022 }} but was waived on October 15.{{cite web|title=New Orleans Pelicans waive Cheatham, Martin, Plowden, and Smart|url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/new-orleans-pelicans-waive-cheatham-martin-plowden-and-smart|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2022|access-date=October 15, 2022}} On November 4, 2022, Plowden was named to the opening night roster for the [[Birmingham Squadron]].{{cite web|title=Birmingham Squadron Announce Opening Night Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/birmingham-squadron-announce-opening-night-roster/n-5895676|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}} Plowden joined the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Thunder Announces 2023 Summer League Roster|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release-summerleague-230701|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2023|access-date=July 8, 2023}} ===Osceola Magic (2023–2024)=== On September 7, 2023, Plowden's rights were traded to the [[Osceola Magic]]{{cite web|title=Osceola Magic Acquire Returning Player Rights For Daeqwon Plowden|url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/osceola-magic-acquire-returning-player-rights-for-daeqwon-plowden|website=NBA.com|date=September 7, 2023|access-date=September 8, 2023}} and on October 18, he signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Sign Free Agent Daeqwon Plowden|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-sign-free-agent-daeqwon-plowden-waive-miye-oni-20231018|website=NBA.com|date=October 18, 2023|access-date=October 19, 2023}} However, he was waived on October 21{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Waive Mac McClung, Daeqwon Plowden and Brandon Williams|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-waive-mac-mcclung-daeqwon-plowden-brandon-williams-20231021|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 21, 2023}} and on November 2, he joined Osceola.{{cite web|title=Training Camp Roster Just Dropped|url=https://osceola.gleague.nba.com/news/training-camp-roster-just-dropped|website=NBA.com|date=November 2, 2023|access-date=December 3, 2023}} On July 16, 2024, Plowden signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Golden State Warriors]],{{cite web|title=Warriors Sign Guard Daeqwon Plowden to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-guard-daeqwon-plowden-to-two-way-contract-20240716|website=NBA.com|date=July 16, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}} but was waived on September 24.{{cite web|title=Warriors Waive Guard Daeqwon Plowden|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-daeqwon-plowden-20240924|website=NBA.com|date=September 24, 2024|access-date=September 24, 2024}} ===Atlanta Hawks / College Park Skyhawks (2024–2025)=== On September 27, 2024, Plowden signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]],{{cite tweet|first=Zach|last=Langley|title=The Atlanta Hawks have officially announced the signing of Daeqwon Plowden.|number=1839817805127958905|user=langleyatl|date=September 27, 2024|access-date=September 28, 2024}} but was waived on October 18.{{cite web|first=Rory|last=Maher|title=Hawks Waive Kevon Harris, Daeqon Plowden|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/hawks-waive-kevon-harris-daeqon-plowden.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 18, 2024|access-date=October 20, 2024}} Eight days later, he joined the [[College Park Skyhawks]]{{cite web|title=College Park Skyhawks Finalize Training Camp Schedule and Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/college-park-skyhawks-finalize-training-camp-schedule-and-roster/n-6159937|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 27, 2024}} and on December 27, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Hawks.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Daeqwon Plowden to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-daeqwon-plowden-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2024|access-date=December 27, 2024}} On January 15, 2025, Plowden made his NBA debut where he made his first seven field goal attempts and finished the game with 19 points in a 110–94 victory over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web|url=https://x.com/NBA/status/1879728306888593822|title=Have a debut, Daeqwon Plowden! He started 7-7 from the field with 5 3PM in his first NBA game 🎯 |date=January 15, 2025|website=x.com}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401705129|title=Atlanta Hawks vs. Chicago Bulls |date=January 15, 2025|website=espn.com}} On July 6, 2025, Plowden was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] as part of a seven-team trade; but was subsequently waived by the team.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/phoenix-suns-acquire-dillon-brooks-jalen-green-and-draft-rights-to-khaman-maluach-rasheer-fleming-and-koby-brea-in-seven-team-trade|title=PHOENIX SUNS ACQUIRE DILLON BROOKS, JALEN GREEN AND DRAFT RIGHTS TO KHAMAN MALUACH, RASHEER FLEMING AND KOBY BREA IN SEVEN-TEAM TRADE|work=NBA.com (Suns)|date=July 6, 2025|quote=The Suns also acquired guard Daeqwon Plowden from the Atlanta Hawks in the trade, who was subsequently waived.}} === Sacramento / Stockton Kings (2025–present) === On July 30, 2025, Plowden signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{cite web | title=Sacramento Kings Sign Daeqwon Plowden to Two-Way Contract | website=NBA | date=2025-07-30 | url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/sacramento-kings-sign-daeqon-plowden-to-two-way-contract | access-date=2025-12-06}} On March 19, 2026, Plowden recorded a career-high 20 points paired with two rebounds and one assist in a 139–118 loss to the [[2025–26 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web|title=Kings' Daeqwon Plowden: Hits for career-high 20 in loss|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-daeqwon-plowden-hits-for-career-high-20-in-loss/|access-date=April 10, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} He made 32 appearances (including seven starts) for Sacramento during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 10.8 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.3 assists. On July 3, 2026, Plowden re-signed with the Kings on a two-year, $5.1 million contract.{{Cite web |date=July 3, 2026 |title=Sacramento Kings Sign Daeqwon Plowden
